target.title: feat: add durable routines registry
target.body:
Closes #98515

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw has cron jobs, tasks, heartbeat, commitments, and channel/session delivery primitives, but no first-class durable registry for recurring team-operations routines. Operators can schedule work today, but they cannot create, inspect, pause, delete, or recover a typed routine as one durable product object with ownership, delivery target, run status, and replay-safe mutation semantics.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds the smallest complete routine slice: a typed routine registry backed by the shared SQLite state DB, Gateway RPC methods, CLI entrypoints, and a schedule trigger that delegates execution to the canonical cron service rather than creating a second scheduler. The design keeps cron as the scheduler owner and routines as the durable registry owner, with internal create/toggle stages so retries recover safely after partial persistence or scheduler failures.

Non-goals for this draft: no Control UI yet, no channel-watch/repository-event/webhook triggers yet, no duplicate scheduler, and no transcript attachment. The trigger model is shaped so those future triggers can share the same routine subsystem instead of growing a second path.

AI-assisted implementation and review were used for this draft PR.

## User Impact

Users and operators can now use `openclaw routines` or Gateway RPC to create, list, inspect, enable, disable, and delete durable scheduled routines. Routine inspection shows owner, delivery target, enabled/deleted state, last and next run visibility, status, and last error context. Repeated create/toggle/delete calls are idempotent, and restart/replay behavior preserves the intended routine state instead of silently losing a schedule toggle or rolling scheduler state backward.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `0c181be14d7eb1a25a8f76ae8473876d554add4a`, rebased on `origin/main` `eb417fa206e6ec76df12c500d08f8fd8691298e9`.
- LOC gate after final trim: total 40 files `+5974/-330`; production 21 files `+2864/-312`, tests 7 files `+2442/-0`, docs 8 files `+343/-18`, generated 4 files `+325/-0`. The broad surface stays cohesive because the registry, schema, Gateway/CLI entrypoints, cron delegation, staged replay, docs, and regression tests are one first-class routine slice.
- Focused local Vitest passed:
  `env PATH=/Users/steipete/.cache/codex-runtimes/codex-primary-runtime/dependencies/node/bin:/Users/steipete/.cache/codex-runtimes/codex-primary-runtime/dependencies/bin:$PATH node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/routines/service.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/routines.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/cron.validation.test.ts src/cli/routines-cli.test.ts src/agents/tools/gateway.test.ts src/cron/service/store.test.ts src/cron/service/ops.persistence-rollback.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/routines.schema.test.ts`
- Focused local lint/boundary proof passed:

- Testbox-through-Crabbox build passed on exact head with provider `blacksmith-testbox`, id `tbx_01kwfv6ng2p22603pxkh2jafya`, Actions run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28550604009:
  `env PATH=/Users/steipete/.local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/Users/steipete/.cache/codex-runtimes/codex-primary-runtime/dependencies/node/bin:/Users/steipete/.cache/codex-runtimes/codex-primary-runtime/dependencies/bin:$PATH node scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs run --provider blacksmith-testbox --blacksmith-org openclaw --blacksmith-workflow .github/workflows/ci-check-testbox.yml --blacksmith-job check --blacksmith-ref main --idle-timeout 90m --ttl 240m --timing-json -- corepack pnpm build`

The proof built the branch, started an isolated local Gateway, approved staged device scopes through `openclaw devices approve`, then drove `openclaw routines list/create/list/get/disable/enable/delete` through the public CLI and Gateway RPC. Final redacted assertion output:
  ```text
  {"routineId":"proof-daily","cronJobId":"routine-cron-61f944366f18f9191d29a9b0425f6694","backing":"linked","status":"enabled","deleted":true}
  ```
- Testbox-through-Crabbox changed gate is currently blocked by an unrelated current-main typecheck failure in `src/commands/daemon-install-helpers.test.ts`, which this branch does not touch. Provider `blacksmith-testbox`, id `tbx_01kwfv6jqk0hgnm7h8vh45v2te`, Actions run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28550601991 failed at `typecheck core tests` with missing `baseUrl` / `SecretRef` shape errors from `fix(install): preserve SecretRef service env values (#96065)`.
- Fresh autoreview against `origin/main` passed clean on exact head with model `koffing-updated`, extra-high reasoning. It explicitly reassessed best-fix fit, owner boundaries, LOC pressure, staged replay, scheduler ownership, delivery defaults, duplicate helper risk, and split-vs-cohesive scope; result: no accepted/actionable findings.
- GitHub PR check rollup for exact head is pass/skip only at the time of this draft update; the PR remains draft and unmerged.

Risks and review focus: routine persistence and cron mutation ordering, idempotent replay after partial failures, schema/client drift, schedule-only routine views over mutable cron backing jobs, and delivery target defaults. No UI screenshot evidence is included because this draft intentionally defers Control UI work.
